newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs sharply off as Nikkei surges.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs sharply off as Nikkei surges.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures fell sharply in Tuesday morning trade as Tokyo stocks shot through the roof following the Dow's impressive overnight close.
The key December Euroyen contract stood at 98.93 at 0340 GMT, one tick above its morning low, against an IMM close at 99.00. Volume was an active 14,920 lots.
June JGBs were at 124.40 after falling as low as 124.30 against a previous 125.46.
The 225-share Nikkei average was up 706.47 to 20,221.22.

Talk of a large Tokyo corporate bond issue of 300 billion yen and a JGB auction later in the week sparked concerns about excess supply and pulled JGB futures down early in the day, a dealer with a European futures house said.
"The Nikkei went above 20,000 and is staying firm and that's an added reason why the JGBs were sold down," he said.
He said both institutions and locals were good sellers and stop-loss sales were triggered around 124.80 after a huge sell order went through at that level in Tokyo, and at 124.50.

Dealers said there was growing talk of investors switching from JGB futures to Nikkei futures, given the stock market's bullish performance in recent weeks and the likelihood of a Japanese rate hike by year end.
The dealer said there was likely to be some short-covering later in the day.
"The fall was a bit too drastic this morning. December Euroyen should stay supported around 98.92 unless the JGBs continue to go down, in which case we'll see 98.88," he said.
